extracted.intended_audience: general readers and film fans seeking encyclopedic information about the film
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic Wikipedia article summarizing the 2009 bromantic comedy film I Love You, Man, including plot, cast, production, reception, box office, soundtrack, and awards. Intended as a comprehensive reference entry about this single film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead performances and chemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: The film 'makes the most of its simple premise due to the heartfelt and hilarious performances of Paul Rudd and Jason Segel.' Entertainment Weekly praised Rudd's performance, and several reviews note the 'camaraderie and undeniable chemistry' between the leads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should consider how convincingly the principal actors portray friendship and comic timing; reviewers attribute much of the film's success to the leads' performances and their chemistry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception (aggregators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotten Tomatoes approval rating of 82% (average 6.9/10) and Metacritic weighted average score of 70/100, indicating 'generally favorable' reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use aggregator scores as a summary metric of critical response; the article cites both Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic values and the Rotten Tomatoes critical consensus statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reception (surveys)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audiences surveyed by CinemaScore gave the film an average grade of 'B+' on a scale of A+ to F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience polling (CinemaScore) is presented separately from critic aggregates and should be used to gauge general viewer satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office and financial performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The film grossed approximately $92 million on a $40 million budget (opening weekend $17.8 million), stayed in the US box-office top ten for five weeks, and ranked among 2009 releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess commercial success via gross vs. budget, opening weekend, longevity in top rankings, and domestic vs. international split; the article reports these concrete figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot, structure, and pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Some critics described the plot as 'formulaic' and the pace of the relationship development as 'rushed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the narrative structure and pacing effectively develop characters and relationships; reviewers here cite formulaic plotting and rushed relationship pacing as criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of bromance / authenticity of friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics differed: some praised the film's 'heartfelt' bromance, while others called it a 'watered-down false bromance' and felt the relationship seemed 'rushed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how authentically the film portrays male friendship and whether emotional beats ring true; the depiction of the central friendship is a recurring evaluative point in reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone, rating, and comedic raunchiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Director John Hamburg said he kept the film R-rated to 'discuss sex' and include elements (e.g., 'blowjobs') that wouldn't fit PG-13; People described the film as 'blush-worthy bawdiness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the appropriateness and impact of the film's adult content and tone on comedic effect; the director frames R-rated material as part of making the film feel 'real.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting and actor fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Casting choices (Rudd and Segel's third collaboration) are noted as contributing to the film's humor; a critic remarked Sydney's role 'seemed to be written for Owen Wilson.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how casting choices and established actor chemistry influence performance and audience expectations; the article emphasizes casting background and collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script development and realism
rubrics_metrics.description: The original script (Let's Be Friends by Larry Levin) sat unused for about 11 years; Hamburg rewrote it 'to make it as real as possible' based on personal experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the screenplay's origins and the filmmakers' intent to ground the story in realism; production history is cited as explanatory context for creative choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music and soundtrack involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The soundtrack (released March 17, 2009) features artists including Rush, Vampire Weekend, The Black Keys, and a cameo by Rush as themselves; Rush's participation was presented as a 'loving tribute' rather than mockery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the role of music and artist involvement in tone and authenticity; the band's cameo and soundtrack selection are highlighted as meaningful production elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominated for Best Kiss at the 2009 MTV Movie Awards and for 'Outstanding Film – Wide Release' at the 21st GLAAD Media Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use awards and nominations as indicators of industry and community recognition; the article lists these specific nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production, distribution, and home media details
rubrics_metrics.description: Produced by DreamWorks, De Line Pictures, Bernard Gayle Productions, and The Montecito Picture Company; distributed by Paramount Pictures (US release March 20, 2009). DVD/Blu-ray released August 11, 2009 with extensive extras (including a full 'Limelight' performance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider production companies, release strategy, and home-media extras when evaluating the film's market positioning and value to fans; the article includes concrete release and extras information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controversy / public response beyond critics
rubrics_metrics.description: A lawsuit was filed in Egypt claiming offense over a dog's name in the film (named after Anwar Sadat); Egyptian bloggers registered complaints and the case sought an apology from the US embassy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into account cultural or legal controversies that affect public perception; the article documents a notable external complaint tied to the film's content.
